claims.claim: Reported earnings for the second quarter of 2026 were $12.1 billion, or $6.11 per diluted share.
Prior-year-period (2Q 2025) reported earnings were $2.5 billion.
Adjusted earnings exclude special items and foreign currency effects.
Adjusted earnings for the second quarter of 2026 totaled $12.0 billion, or $6.06 per diluted share.
Cash flow from operations was $22.6 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
Cash flow from operations was $8.6 billion in the second quarter of 2025.
Free cash flow was $18.1 billion for the second quarter of 2026.
Adjusted free cash flow was $15.4 billion for the second quarter of 2026.
Upstream earnings were $8.2 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
Upstream results were supported by record U.S. production.
Upstream results were supported by higher liquids realizations.

The release does not provide specific financial guidance or outlook for future quarters.
The release notes that Chevron publishes a "Sensitivities and Forward Guidance" document updated quarterly on its website.
Chevron signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Microsoft to provide 2.67 gigawatts of behind-the-meter power for a West Texas data center.
The Microsoft agreement positions the company to generate resilient cash flows through this new energy business.
claims.note: The release's "resilient cash flows" language is a general CEO quote about leveraging the company's unique capabilities and powering American AI, not tied to the PPA as a cash-flow source; the release also never classifies the power agreement as a "new energy business" (its only reference to new energies businesses is a separate boilerplate strategy statement).

claims.claim: The company aims to reduce structural costs by $3 billion to $4 billion by the end of 2026.
Total debt was reduced by a record $8.4 billion in the second quarter of 2026.
Total debt was $37.1 billion at June 30, 2026.
The net debt-to-CFFO ratio was 0.6x at June 30, 2026.
The net debt-to-CFFO ratio was 0.8x in the second quarter of 2025, so the ratio improved year-over-year.
Chevron declared a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share.
The dividend is payable September 10, 2026 to common stockholders of record as of August 19, 2026.
International upstream production faced curtailments in the Partitioned Zone between Saudi Arabia and Kuwait due to the Middle East conflict.
